messages:
From: Elena Park <elena.park@theranova.health>
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.example.com
Cc: DPO Team <dpo@theranova.health>
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Quick Q on geo commitments and temporary cross-hop during burst

Hi Tessa,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — product looked solid. Before we move to procurement we need to confirm a few things for our security and legal review so we can sign the DPA addendum:

- Can Redwood commit to region-specific processing for PII in our EU and APAC environments (i.e., not leaving EU data in US compute except for defined transient windows)?
- What is your policy for transient cross-region processing during capacity bursts or maintenance? We need the maximum window and notification SLA.
- Who are your subprocessors for logging/analytics and edge caching in APAC? We require a roster and whether they have access to encryption keys.
- KMS model: do you support customer-managed keys for EU-only volumes or only split-KMS?

I'm attaching a short spreadsheet with the items our DPO flagged (TheraNova-DPA-questions.xlsx). If you can send a mutual action plan and an initial DPA draft we can route it internally.

Cheers,

Elena Park
Head of Security & Privacy
TheraNova Health


From: tessa_morgan@redwood.example.com
To: Elena Park <elena.park@theranova.health>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.example.com, marissa_cole@redwood.example.com
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 11:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Quick Q on geo commitments and temporary cross-hop during burst

Elena — thanks for the clear list. Looping Kim (Legal) and Marissa (Privacy) to confirm contract language and ops constraints. High level answers below and a proposed MAP (mutual action plan) in-line:

1) Region-specific processing: yes — Redwood can pin tenant workloads to region groups (EU / APAC / US). We offer an EU-only placement option for data-in-flight and persistent storage. The DPA addendum can specify EU placement for TheraNova production workloads.

2) Transient cross-region processing: standard policy is a 48-hour max transient window in exceptional burst or incident scenarios; to be used only after attempting local capacity scaling, and with automated notification to the customer. Ops will propose a 72-hour carve-out only in agreed exceptional cases — we need this approved by Legal.

3) Subprocessors: we maintain an up-to-date roster; we can provide an exported CSV of subprocessors for analytics, logging, and CDN/edge partners. None of those subprocessors are allowed access to customer plaintext data without KMS key material; access is controlled via tokenized belts in the runtime.

4) KMS: we support customer-managed KMS in EU regions (BYOK) for data-at-rest and for encrypting snapshots. We also have a split-KMS model for additional assurance.

Mutual action plan (proposed):
- Day 0: Redwood provides DPA draft + subprocessor roster export (attached Redwood-DPA-draft-v1.pdf).
- Day 2: TheraNova returns marked DPA comments and KMS requirements.
- Day 5: Legal alignment call to resolve transient-hop window (48h vs 72h) and KMS binding.
- Day 12: Execute DPA addendum and confirm onboarding date.

Attachments: Redwood-DPA-draft-v1.pdf (DPA draft), I will attach the subprocessor CSV once Legal confirms the export level.

If that MAP looks good I'll open a HubSpot deal stage update (TN-4771) and add the DocuSign link.

Best,

Tessa Morgan
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Kim / Marissa — forwarding TheraNova's questions and my proposed MAP. Key legal asks:

- Approve or propose edits to transient cross-region window: Ops suggests 48h standard, 72h exceptional with sign-off. Is 72h acceptable if we carve it as "customer-approved exceptional event" and require post-event report?
- Confirm that BYOK for EU is contractually enforceable and whether we need to add specific key-escrow language for long-term retention scenarios.

Notes from ops: we will not permit subprocessors to hold customer plaintext; all access requires KMS gating. The subprocessor roster will include CDN edge names used for APAC cache.

Please reply inline — I want to get this back to Elena by EOD Tuesday.

Thanks,
Tessa

From: kimberly_park@redwood.example.com

Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 15:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Quick Q on geo commitments and temporary cross-hop during burst

Tessa / Marissa — quick take from Legal:

- Transient window: we should offer 48 hours as standard, and allow a documented exceptional extension to 72 hours but only if the customer signs the DPA addendum language that describes the conditions (capacity surge, emergency maintenance) and requires an incident follow-up report within 72 hours of any extended cross-hop. That balances operational flexibility and auditability.
- BYOK: acceptable. Add clause that customer-managed keys must be provisioned in the customer KMS and that Redwood will not retain copies of key material. For very long retention (>2y) we suggest a clause that covers key rotation responsibilities and snapshot encryption binding.
- Subprocessor export: ops can share the full roster. Redact internal contact emails but include company name, region, and access scope. Also include a one-line attestation per subprocessor that they do not hold plaintext without KMS gating.

I attach suggested redlines for the DPA (appended to Redwood-DPA-draft-v1.pdf) and a sample clause for the exceptional transient window. Once you prepare the redlined PDF I'll review and we can send to Elena.

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference
